title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Rule on the Benefit Year, Exhaustion and Closure
content:
**1. Benefit year.** The benefit year of an Unemployment Benefit Claims record begins on the claim effective date, which is the Sunday of the week the claim was filed or backdated to, and the benefit year end date is the Saturday that ends the program's benefit year length counted from that Sunday.

**2. Exhaustion.** A claim is exhausted when a payment brings its remaining balance to zero; an exhausted claim accepts no further weekly payments, and the claimant may then be considered for a later program under the Department's program sequencing rules.

**3. Closure.** A claim is closed at its benefit year end date whatever its status, except a claim already withdrawn.

**4. Weeks around the end date.** Weeks ending after the benefit year end date are never paid on that claim, while weeks ending on or before it remain payable after closure when they were certified in time.

**5. Balance.** A balance left on a closed claim is not carried into a new claim.

## Derived dates

| Benefit year length | Hypothetical effective date (Sunday) | Benefit year end date (Saturday) |
|---|---|---|
| 52 weeks | Sunday 4 January 2026 | Saturday 2 January 2027 |
| 26 weeks | Sunday 4 January 2026 | Saturday 4 July 2026 |

## Points of judgement

- A week ending on the benefit year end date itself is a week ending on or before it, and remains payable after closure when it was certified in time.
- A week ending the Saturday after the benefit year end date is never paid on that claim.
- A claim already withdrawn is not closed at its benefit year end date.
